usageNotes: Use this to audit which disks within a cluster backup job are actually being backed up and why — useful for verifying that no critical volumes are excluded due to misconfiguration. Requires `Sys.Audit` on `/` (cluster-wide scope), so API tokens scoped to individual nodes will not work. The response is structured as a two-level tree (guests → volumes) intended for tree-view UIs; parse `children[*].children` to programmatically check each volume's `included` and `reason` fields.

examples.summary: Check which volumes are included for backup job 'daily-all'

tips: Guests with type 'unknown' are VMs/CTs that have been removed from the cluster but not purged from the backup job — they will appear in results but have no live configuration.

A volume with included=false will show a human-readable reason string explaining the exclusion (e.g. 'drive is marked to be excluded', 'backup disabled for this guest'); use this to distinguish intentional vs. unintentional exclusions.

This endpoint reflects the current job configuration, not historical backup results — a volume marked included=true means it is configured to be backed up on the next run, not that it was successfully backed up previously.
